text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- Romanian carpet production in decline because of low prices of imported carpets.
- Bankruptcy has not become yet part of the treatment needed to heal Romania's economy, the newspaper says.
- Unemployment and inflation will not spare Romania, Industry Minister Calin Tariceanu says in interview.
ADEVARUL
- The Senate's economic commission endorsed a proposal to cut profit tax from present 38 percent to 30 percent.
- SNCFR rail authority plans to raise tariffs starting February 17.
- The Agriculture Ministry said the price of bread might double within the next three months.
- The court of accounts decided to block bank accounts of regie autonome from the Jiu Valley coalfield due to its huge debts, the paper said.
- The Defence Ministry's budget will amount to 3.11 percent of GDP.
- Distribution of credits to the farming sector proceeds at slow pace, the paper says.
- Central bank governor Mugur Isarescu asked the Senate to speed up amendments to present financial legislation.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The big Alfa trade union bloc asked for a minimum monthly wage of 180,000 lei, up from government's offer of 130,000 lei.
- Romanian companies failed to cash export earnings worth some $500,000 in 1996.
- Romanian exports to the United States will amount to $350 million this year.
General:
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- The tenants' association will stage a protest outside the government's building on Febaruary 21, over changes brought to the law of restitution of houses seized by former Communists. The group timed their protest to coincide with the opening of French President Jacques Chirac's visit.
- France's Hachette sounds local business opportunities, has talks with Romania's main press distributor, Rodipet SA.
- Romanian Foreign Ministry experts are looking into ways to unblock treaty talks with Russia.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Foreign Ministry is planning moral and material redress for Romanian diplomats persecuted by ousted communists.
- Newspaper prints excerpts from prosecutors' report on crimes prosecuted in Romania in 1996.
ADEVARUL
- The wife and brother of miners' leader Miron Cosma urged President Emil Constantinescu to intervene to have Cosma freed from detention and tried at liberty.

- The head of Romania's Intelligence Service (SRI) Virgil Magureanu told Senate commission that his institution was ready to open access to files of the communist-era Securitate secret police if parliament decides to scrap 40-year ban on access, paper says in report on legal commission hearing.
- The head of Romania's counter-intelligence service (SIE), which operates only abroad, discussed prospects of bringing SIE under parliament control during commission hearing, paper says.
ZIUA
- Former King Michael will regain his Romanian citizenship, paper says on report that government promised to take steps to cancel 1848 decree which stripped Michael of his citizenship.
- Newspaper reports on row splitting the heads of Romania's revived masonic lodges.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
